_note: Every gameplay number lives here. Nothing tunable should be a const in a .gd file any more. tools/sim.gd plays hundreds of days against this file and prints the curves, so a change here can be checked without playing.
_contract: THE BALANCE CONTRACT. tools/sim.gd measures these from SIMULATED play, and tests/run.gd asserts them. The previous version asserted hand-set state, which is how a grade model broken in four places passed 218 tests.
bare room, perfect teaching  -> ~0.63  a C
full room, never helped      -> ~0.71  a C
full room, perfect teaching  -> ~0.97  an A
Homework is a bonus on top, so a good term survives one bad lesson.

grade_bands._note: Where a numeric grade (0..1) lands as a letter. Used to hardcode as A>=0.88, B>=0.75, C>=0.62, D>=0.50, E>=0.38 -- the contract's own bare-room-perfect-teaching row (0.63) sat 1 point above the C floor, and realistic imperfect play (not perfect, just decent) landed BELOW it, in D. Softened so the same three contract scenarios keep their letters with real margin instead of a hair's width, and so trying-but-imperfect play actually reads as a C rather than a D. Below 'e' is an F.
grade_bands._contract_check: bare-room-perfect (0.63) and full-room-never-helped (0.71) must both stay C -- so 'c' must sit below both and 'b' must sit above both. full-room-perfect (0.97) must stay A.

lesson._note: work_seconds is how much UNSTUCK time a student needs to finish. lesson_seconds is the clock you are racing. A stalled student's timer freezes, so an unreached student simply never finishes — that is the whole pressure.
lesson._supplies_note: A materials day (DayEvent "supplies") starts every seated child empty-handed, and it is the teacher's job to hand their things out before the bell. A child who never got theirs works at this fraction of the normal rate for the day -- a PACE penalty on their own work, exactly like room.cluster_penalty, never a term on their grade. It cannot fire unless the day rolled the materials event, which tools/sim.gd never does, so the contract rows never see it.
lesson._uncollected_note: Seconds a finished sheet may sit on a desk before the game says out loud, once per run, that it only counts when collected. Uncollected work HALVES that child's lesson grade at the bell (see grade.uncollected_penalty), and nothing said so. Not instant: the player may already be walking over, and a nudge that fires the moment a child finishes would be noise rather than teaching.

class._desk_note: A desk is a SEAT you bought, and the class grows into it. The cap was hard-wired at 8 from the beginning -- eight desks in a 20x11 room, and no way to have more. Buying one costs coins AND floor: a desk needs two free tiles with an aisle to the door, so a bigger room is what makes a bigger class possible rather than a number in a table.

homework._note: not_done_forgiveness: a student who misses homework is asked again the next night rather than being locked out forever.

room_upkeep._note: Daily clutter -- trash and spills, scripts/interact/mess.gd. Legwork with a flat coin tip, not a grade input: nothing here touches grade/room_base or anything the balance contract measures, so it is exempt from that contract on purpose.

term._note: A run is as many terms as you can keep the job for, not one term. Each term is still 'days' long and ends in an exam scored on everything built up so far; passing 'target_base'/'target_growth' opens the next term with the room, curriculum, coins and teacher level carried forward (see _next_term_note) -- only the roster resets. The run ends when a term's target is missed.
term._exam_note: The exam is a child's own record, plus a little for the room you sat them in. It used to be average*0.75 + room*0.35, which counted the room TWICE -- room_score is already inside every daily grade -- and marked down everyone whose average was above 0.39. A child who averaged an A all term sat the exam in a bare room and got a B.
term._next_term_note: What survives a term. The ROOM you built, the curriculum you learned, your own level and perks, and your coins all carry over -- they are the things you spent the term making, and taking them away would make the term a sandbox rather than a chapter. What does NOT carry is the class: children who passed move up and out, and children who did not stay for another go, keeping their record.
term._target_note: How many children must pass for you to keep the job. It rises every term, and it is the only thing in the game you can LOSE to. Without it the room gets better every term against a difficulty that never moves, so by the third term nothing you do matters. The target is what makes a better room necessary rather than merely pleasant.

upkeep._note: Furniture needs replacing. A per-item daily cost means coins never just pile up, and a huge room you cannot afford is a real decision.

teacher._note: The teacher's own numbers. speed and pick_radius used to be consts in actor.gd/interactable.gd -- they were missed when everything else moved here, because they read as physics rather than balance. They live here now so perks can raise them and tools/sim.tscn can model a levelled teacher.
teacher._dash_note: The dash replaced the old held 'Hurry' sprint (const SPRINT in actor.gd). Trigger it by double-tapping a direction within dash_double_tap_window of the first press, or with the dedicated dash action (Shift) -- either fires the same burst in your current heading, then it is on cooldown -- the cooldown is the whole limiter, there is no stamina. dash_duration seconds at dash_speed_multiplier times normal speed, then dash_duration+dash_cooldown before the next one. Crossing the room is still a real cost; a dash spends the wait between dashes to shave a corner, not to glide the whole way. The cooldown is long enough on purpose for the HUD's cooldown meter (hud.gd _update_status()) to mean something -- a near-instant recharge reads as permanently full.
teacher._dash_cancel_note: Dash-cancel: for dash_cancel_grace seconds AFTER a burst ends, the teacher's interaction reach is widened by dash_cancel_reach px, so a dash that lands just short of a desk still lets you press E on it -- the burst 'connects' into the action instead of dying a tile away. Pure reach: it changes nothing a delegated room is graded on, only how forgiving the arrival is, and only for a blink after a real dash.
teacher._dash_lane_note: Furniture lanes. An item tagged "lane" in the items table (the Reading Rug) makes the walkable tiles beside it a clean runway -- dashing there lets the burst carry, up to dash_lane_extend extra seconds spread across one dash. An item tagged "clutter" (the Storage Crate, the Beanbag) makes the tiles beside it tight: a dash through them dies on the spot and dash_clutter_penalty seconds are added to the cooldown. It is all layout -- a well-arranged room has clear runs, a cluttered one makes you weave -- and it touches nothing a room is graded on.
teacher._dash_smoke_note: The dash's smoke. Decoration only -- spawned off the engine's own randf() and never Game.rng, the rule every Fx effect follows, so a replay of the same seed still matches. Here rather than as consts in fx.gd because the light_feet perk scales all of it: a levelled dash kicks up more smoke, wider, in bigger motes, and that is most of how the upgrade reads on screen.
teacher._chain_dash_note: The chain dash, taught by the mentor (Game.chain_dash_taught). A dash that reaches a child with their hand visibly up answers them on arrival -- the same help() the E key gives, no stopping to press it. The burst ends there, and the wait before the next dash drops to chain_dash_cooldown, so the next hand can be run at straight away: hand to hand to hand. Only a VISIBLE hand counts (a Quiet child hiding a stall still has to be noticed and walked to), only one child per dash, and only a desk within chain_dash_reach px that lies ahead of the teacher, so a dash away from someone never answers them. After chain_dash_max_links answers in a row the refund stops and the ordinary cooldown applies. chain_dash_window is how long after one answer the next still counts toward the same chain (the floater count). Pace only: it helps exactly the children E would have, so nothing a room is graded on moves.

skip._note: Teaching on your own -- the teacher hands the room over and lets the days run. Each skipped day is resolved by RoomSim under the Steady policy, the SAME model a delegated room runs and the same one Game.auto_teach already uses for a single lesson; nothing here is a formula that awards a grade. What makes it a real decision rather than a free fast-forward: no homework is set on a day you were not there to set it, so the marking that lifts a class never happens, and RoomSim Steady is a competent stand-in rather than you at your best. max_days is the cap as shipped. item_bonus_cap is how much furniture may add on top of it later -- an item def with a "skip_days" key contributes, the way "teaches" already grants a concept; no item carries one yet, which is why the hook is capped rather than open.

student._note: Students improve just by being taught. A level nudges aptitude and diligence a little; ready_level is when they can be sent up. XP STOPS at ready_level+hold_grace: a child kept long past readiness has learned what you can teach them, which is a soft cost for holding them back rather than a punishment.

concepts._note: What knowing your material is worth. It scales with how much of the lesson the child actually got through, so it rewards TEACHING rather than merely turning up: a class you never went near gains almost nothing from your expertise. Small per concept and capped, and worth zero on day one, which is what keeps the three-row contract unmoved.

pacing._note: Ten-commits.md step 3: whether the curriculum is moving at a pace the term can actually finish on, since nothing before this told you either way. Measured against how many NEW concepts this term itself has unlocked (concepts carry over term to term -- see Game.term_start_concepts -- so the whole curriculum's total is the wrong yardstick). Coins and XP only, paid at the bell, alongside the day's ordinary payout -- never a grade term, so the three-row contract cannot move and needs no new guard.

events._note: Ten-commits.md step 5: the ordinary-day spread guarantee. `none` is still the single biggest slice of the table by weight, but two of it in a row is the ceiling -- the third day after a streak that long rerolls with `none` excluded entirely, so a term can never serve twenty ordinary days back to back the way the raw weights alone would allow.

room._note: Buying floor space, and how it is used. Floor is priced per TILE of new floor and rising with each expansion, so a bigger room is a real investment rather than a thing you tick off on day two. The room only grows right and down: the door is a fixed point on the left wall and everything already placed must keep its coordinates. cluster_penalty is the counter to the discovered meta of cramming every desk into the middle: a child with another occupied desk orthogonally adjacent works this fraction slower. The opening layout has no two seats within one tile of each other, so it costs nothing until a player moves desks together. Layout-only -- never touches a grade formula, and the contract sim (tools/sim.gd _one_lesson()) never sees it: it sets every seat to 0 and calls tick_work() directly rather than through the room.

test._note: The end-of-unit test. Playable only after you have taught the unit enough times to have unlocked its concepts. It is the one instrument you cannot intervene in: no helping, no collecting, no stalls. What it measures is the classroom you BUILT and the children you developed, not how well you ran round the room today -- which is exactly why it is worth more than a lesson.

quiz._note: The in-lesson diagnostic. Carries NO direct grade weight on purpose -- the three-row balance contract is measured without one, and a quiz that paid grade would quietly move the pillar. What it buys is information: who is behind, while there is still lesson left to do something about it. It costs 14 of a 45-second lesson, raised from 10 after the term simulator showed quizzing paying about ten times the coins at an identical grade -- which is not a decision, it is a formality.
quiz._buff_note: A quiz cost 14 of a 45-second lesson and returned 1.5s of work per student plus 6s per flagged child -- break-even at about four students on time alone, and nothing of it survived the bell. It now leaves the class FOCUSED for the rest of the lesson: they have just been made to think, so they get stuck less. That is the retrieval-practice claim the 1.5s was already gesturing at, made into something you can feel.

answer_all._note: The mass-help skill, on its own key (J). One press does what walking to every stuck desk and pressing E would: clears confusion, resolves the flagged quizzes -- the same per-child effects, compressed. Like the quiz it pays NO grade and NO coins, so it cannot move the three-row contract; tests/run.gd test_balance() guards that tools/sim.gd never calls it. The whole cost is seconds_cost off the lesson clock (steeper than the quiz's -- this is a panic button) plus cooldown_seconds before it is available again. Re-armed by classroom.start_lesson().

graduation._note: What sending a child up is worth. Scaled by readiness, so graduating someone the moment they qualify pays less than seeing them through.

moments._note: The notable-moments log per student: a short highlight reel of what happened to THIS child, stored as kind ids and rendered to prose at display time so 'prose never numbers' stays easy. cap keeps the first entry plus the most recent ones when it overflows. grade_min_history is how many past grades a child needs before a jump or drop between letter bands counts as a moment. favourite_streak (ten-commits.md step 6) is how many lessons running in their own best subject earns them a moment about it.

coaching._note: Bought from a student's own file. Cost multiplies per purchase FOR THAT CHILD, so the decision is who to invest in rather than levelling everyone flat.

lesson_crafting._note: Cost to craft-attempt a lesson grows per craft_level already banked for THAT lesson (coaching-style). Quality effect is a small multiplier on difficulty_mults(), never a new grade term, capped so a fully-crafted lesson still cannot exceed the existing lesson_cap ceiling -- see Game.difficulty_mults()/craft_work_mult().

quick_sweep.name: Quick Sweep

perk_effects._note: Per RANK. brisk_walk adds to teacher.speed, long_reach to pick_radius, calm_presence multiplies the stall chance of students within its radius, practised_marker removes that many sheets from the nightly pile. quick_sweep subtracts from room_upkeep.clean_presses (floor of 1), carrying_voice adds tiles to voice.range_tiles, quick_study adds a percentage to Game.lesson_length()'s multiplier chain, lucky_break biases Assignments' rarity roll toward rarer tiers, thrifty is a fraction off a shop item's BUY price only (never its sell value), iron_will multiplies (compounding per rank) only the dis_spread term in Game.tick_class() -- trouble still starts from boredom/frustration exactly as often, it just travels less. light_feet is the dash's own upgrade: each rank adds light_feet_duration seconds to the BURST, so the dash covers more ground at the same speed -- speed is brisk_walk's job and doubling up would make the two indistinguishable -- and takes light_feet_cooldown off the wait, floored in Progress so the HUD's cooldown meter never recharges instantly and stops meaning anything. The two smoke terms are pure juice: more and bigger motes per rank, so a levelled dash LOOKS levelled.

_items_note: 'teaches' means owning the item unlocks that concept outright -- which is what finally ties the furniture you buy to the curriculum. 'needs' gates an item behind a concept you must already know, so the shop grows as you teach rather than only as you earn.
_subject_shelf_note: Ten-commits.md step 8: the subject-specific items got their own 'subjects' shop tab, split out of 'learning' where the distinction used to be invisible -- item_order is tested cost-ascending WITHIN a category, so reordering learning itself could never have grouped them; a category of their own does. Two per strand now (ela/math/science/social), each carrying a 'strand' and a 'strand_bonus': it pays its small ordinary 'bonus' on any day, plus strand_bonus on top only when today's lesson matches. Specialising the room makes it do more on its subject and less off it -- never strictly better. It cannot move the 0.63/0.71/0.97 contract: Game.room_score() clamps to room_cap and tools/sim.gd fills the contract room to that cap regardless of which items it uses. See Items.strand()/strand_bonus().

traits._note: One per child, rolled at enrolment and never changed. Every trait has a real mechanical hook -- a trait that only shows up as a line of text on the class list is decoration, and decoration is what makes a player stop reading the list. 'blurb' is what the file says about them; the player is never told the numbers.

disruption._note: Messing about, which is NOT the same as being stuck. A stuck child has stopped and wants you; a disruptive one has stopped and is stopping the children either side of them, and it spreads along the desks until somebody deals with it. Both sources are things the player caused: boredom is finished work you never came to collect, frustration is a child left stuck too long. Neither is bad luck.

flare._note: A flare-up: a random, timed warning that ONE calm child is about to kick off. A bubble goes up over their head with a countdown -- reach the desk and press E (this is what the dash is for: a flare across the room is only catchable if you spend a burst) and it is defused, with a small coin tip and a little XP for the child. Let the countdown run out and they start disrupting -- the ordinary messing-about mechanic, nothing new grade-side. Independent of boredom/frustration on purpose: those already lead to disruption; this is the extra, catchable urgency. onset is per calm seated child per second, multiplied by whatever today's day event does to stall (a Restless class throws more). Capped per day so a bad-luck run cannot bury you.

bell_rush._note: The end-of-session rush: when the lesson ends, hand every child's marked work back before the clock runs out for a flat coin bonus plus a little XP per desk. A recurring reason to use the dash on a room you already know. DISABLED for now (enabled=false) -- it belongs to a later stage of the game, once the single-classroom loop is fully taught -- but built and tested so switching it on is a one-line change, not a new feature. Pure coins + XP: it never touches grade, same as the mess tip and the flare tip.

voice._note: Raising your voice. The only verb in the game that is not attached to a landmark -- but it still depends on WHERE YOU ARE STANDING, because it only reaches desks within earshot. It settles the room; it does not teach anybody anything, so a stuck child still needs you at their desk. That is the line that keeps walking the room the game.

inspection._note: What an inspector actually judges. Three things, and you can prepare for all three, because the visit is announced the evening before -- an unannounced judgement is weather, not a decision. Each is something the game already tracks: the room you built, the lesson they watched, and whether you know the material you are teaching.

_flat_note: 'flat' means the item lies on the floor or hangs on the wall, so it gets no contact shadow -- a rug with a shadow under it looks like it is hovering.

teaching._note: Standing at the front and TEACHING. Work only advances while the class is paying attention, and attention only comes from you. Before this a lesson ran itself and the player's whole job was reacting to bubbles -- there was nothing to DO with the time between them.
teaching._decay_note: Attention DECAYS rather than switching off. As a hard on/off, a two second trip to help one child froze seven others dead, which reads as the game being broken rather than as a trade-off. Decay means a short trip costs a slice of progress and a long absence costs all of it.
teaching._drift_note: How far attention has to fall before the game says out loud, once per run, that work only moves while you are at the front. Deliberately NOT the moment you step away -- walking to a stuck child is the game, and a nudge fired then would read as 'do not do that'. It fires once the absence has actually cost something, which is when the sentence means anything.

mood._note: The class, in a word, on the status strip: the attention bar minus a penalty per child messing about and per child visibly stuck, banded into with you / drifting / restless / lost them. The critique that asked for it: the strip drew attention and voice as ASCII pips, and the one thing a new player needs from the strip -- is the room with me or not -- was arithmetic on a row of bars. Never a number on screen.

difficulty._note: How much a lesson's difficulty rating actually moves. Difficulty 3 is the neutral middle: work_mult and stall_mult are 1.0 there, and each step away from it scales by these amounts. A 1 is noticeably easier to get a class through than a 5, without either being a different game.
difficulty._furniture_note: A furnished desk makes the work EASIER, not just better-marked. room_score used to feed the grade and nothing else, so a bookshelf was worth points and changed nothing you could watch. It now takes the edge off difficulty for whoever sits near it -- which is what the player expects a well-equipped desk to do.

specialism._note: The subject you trained in. Yours is a step easier to get a class through and pays better; everything else is a step harder. A lean, not a cage -- you can teach anything, and sometimes you will have to, because a class that only ever sees one subject learns one subject.

assignments._note: The paper you set. A hand is drawn at the podium and you pick one, so setting work is a decision instead of a formality. RARITY pays -- coins and the experience the children get -- and DIFFICULTY is how long the paper takes. They are rolled separately and then correlated, so a Legendary is usually demanding: the question is whether this class, on this day, can actually finish it. Work you never collect counts for half.
assignments._colour_note: Grey, green, blue, violet, gold -- the ladder every looter has trained players to read without a legend. The names are yours; the order of the colours is the one people already know.
assignments._grade_note: Rarity deliberately pays COINS and XP, never grade. The three-row balance contract is measured from work completion, and a multiplier on the lesson term would move the pillar by luck rather than by play.
assignments._hand_size_note: How many cards are drawn, rolled fresh each morning between hand_size_min and hand_size_max inclusive -- a real shuffle, not always the same count. This is the hook for a later teacher LUCK skill (more, and eventually better, options for a teacher who has earned it) -- do not hardcode a count anywhere else when that lands, read it from here.

autopilot._note: Walks you to whoever needs you next, and back to the front when nobody does. It moves your feet and NEVER presses your buttons -- the judgement of what to do at the desk stays yours, and so does the decision to stop teaching in order to go. It exists because crossing a room you can already see is not the interesting part of this game.

aide._note: A teacher's aide, hired in the staff room and paid every day. They walk the room COLLECTING FINISHED WORK -- the chore -- and they never help, settle or mark. That line is deliberate: collecting is legwork, and helping is a judgement about a particular child. Hiring somebody to do the judgement would be hiring somebody to play the game.
aide._cost_note: The wage is per DAY, so an aide is a standing decision rather than a purchase you make once and forget. In a bad term they are the thing you let go.

janitor._note: Same shape as the aide, one door over: hired in the staff room, paid every day, and they clean the room's own daily mess (mess.gd) FOR you -- one piece per interval, any time of day, not lesson-gated like the aide, because mess isn't either. Same legwork/judgement line: there is no judgement in a spill, so there is nothing here hiring somebody out of.

staff_levels._note: Both the aide and the janitor can be trained up once hired -- E on their row again spends coins to raise their level, which shortens their own interval (collect_seconds / clean_seconds). Same rising-cost-per-level shape as buying a bigger room. Capped at max_level so a levelled aide is faster, never instant.

school._note: Rooms you do not stand in. A delegated room is RESOLVED BY RUNNING THE LESSON with a hired teacher's policy driving it -- the same work, stall, disruption and grade models the player is subject to. A formula would have been far easier and every number it produced would have been a lie the player could not have produced by playing.
school._furniture_note: A delegated room's furniture is bought as a LEVEL rather than placed tile by tile. Placing furniture is a spatial puzzle about range, and the puzzle is only interesting in a room you can see. Buying the outcome is honest about that.

reputation._note: What the school is thought of, 0..100. It is the ONLY thing a badly run room costs you. The simulator showed rooms are straightforwardly profitable -- each one earns more than its wages -- so without this, 'open another room' has an obvious yes and staffing it properly is optional. Reputation is what makes a room you cannot run a liability rather than free money.
reputation._gate_note: It GATES rather than pays: how many rooms you may open, and how good the applicants are. A gate is a better shape than a bonus here -- a bonus would just be more money in a game that already has enough.

ads._note: The optional reward-video poster (scripts/interact/ad_poster.gd). No real ad SDK is connected yet -- wait below is a compressed stand-in for what an actual video would take, tunable independently of the seconds it represents once a real SDK lands (see my-brain/tools.md).

complication._note: One roll-attempt per second while a lesson is running, at onset_per_second times the active term path's own density_mult (see term_paths). Which complication actually fires is decided by scripts/data/complications.gd's own weighted table, the same mechanism DayEvent already uses. Capped per lesson so a bad-luck run cannot bury you -- same reasoning as flare.max_per_day.
complication._boost_note: Answering someone at your desk well can win a stretch of quicker feet. It multiplies TEACHER PACE and nothing else -- never a grade, never a child's record -- because the balance contract measures a perfect teacher against an absent one, and a faster walk cannot move either row. It never stacks; a second win refreshes the timer. The bell ends it.

term_paths._note: The fork at the start of each term, modeled on the assignment hand: a few pre-rolled paths, pick one, the rest are discarded -- but drawn WITHOUT replacement, unlike the daily hand, since repeating a termly choice would read as broken rather than lucky. lesson_mult layers onto Game.lesson_length() and coin_mult onto the day's coin payout, the same way a DayEvent's own multipliers already do -- never into lesson.lesson_seconds itself, so tools/sim.gd's contract rows never see it. density_mult scales complication.onset_per_second for the whole term. ordinary_term sits at 1.0 across every multiplier on purpose: a player who always picks it sees exactly today's numbers.

paths.name: Busy Term
paths.blurb: Longer lessons, more to juggle, better pay.

paths.name: Chaotic Term
paths.blurb: Everything happens at once. Hold it together and it shows in the pay.

bosses._note: The roguelike subject boss. On every boss_term_interval-th term Game.draw_term_paths() folds these cards into the same fork pool the ordinary Quiet/Ordinary/Busy/Chaotic cards are drawn from, tagged kind:"boss" -- a telegraphed choice alongside them, never an ambush. A boss term otherwise plays exactly like an ordinary one (every multiplier 1.0); what changes is the exam. Game.next_term() judges the class AVERAGE that sit_exam() already produced against this card's `target` instead of the seat-count term target. Clear it: award the matching trophy (scripts/data/trophies.gd) and unlock the cosmetic decor gated on any boss trophy. Miss it: run_over, exactly as missing an ordinary term. `target` is on sit_exam()'s own 0..1 grade-average scale.
bosses._fight_note: THE FIGHT (scripts/data/boss_fight.gd). The last day of a boss term is played, not sat: the paper makes one MOVE per round from the card's `moves` list (freeze / chain / noise / present), and each child it touches ends the round rallied (dealt with inside quick_seconds), held (dealt with in time) or dropped (still frozen or shouting, or left alone up front, when the question moved on). finish() turns that into StudentData.boss_delta = rally_mark*rallied - drop_mark*dropped, clamped to +-max_swing, which Game.exam_score_for() adds on top of the child's own record that afternoon. max_swing is about half a letter band on purpose: the record still decides the exam, the day decides the margin. tools/sim.gd never sees any of this (test_boss_fight() scans for it). The composure_* thresholds band the room's kept/resolved ratio into a word for the strip and the report -- never a number on screen.

table.name: Reading Paper
table.tactic: They freeze on the long passages. Stay near whoever reads slowest, and steady them the moment the bubble goes up.
table.blurb: The paper the district sends round. One morning, the whole class.

table.name: Number Gauntlet
table.tactic: One frozen child freezes the next desk along. Spread the desks out before the morning, and break a chain at its first link.
table.blurb: Every child, every fact, against the clock. Nobody may freeze.

table.name: Science Fair
table.tactic: One child at a time presents. Stand with them -- within a desk or two -- and settle the audience when it gets restless.
table.blurb: They explain their own experiments to a room of strangers.

table.name: Mock Election
table.tactic: They argue. Your voice reaches the desks near you; be in the middle of the room, not at the front.
table.blurb: Both sides argued, and the votes counted out in the open.

table.name: Open Evening
table.tactic: Everything at once, in turn. There is no one answer; it is the whole term's teaching, tested on one evening.
table.blurb: Parents, inspectors, the lot. The room has to hold up under it.

table.name: Mock Inspection
table.tactic: The visitor watches the whole room, not just the front row. Keep the noise from spreading before it reaches every desk.
table.blurb: The visit nobody can quite prepare for. Every desk, at once.
